newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's KPC sees no threat from Iraqi oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's KPC sees no threat from Iraqi oil exports.

text.p: Kuwait will maintain its market share despite Iraq's limited return to the oil export market, a Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) official said on Wednesday.
"It (Iraqi supply) will not have an impact," KPC's executive assistant managing director for sales and marketing, Hussain al-Shamm'a told Reuters.
"Our ties with our clients are strong and traditional; they will not be affected by a new barrel coming to the market."
Under the U.N. deal signed in May Iraq will be allowed to sell $2.0 billion worth of crude for a renewable six months period mainly to finance the import of food and medicine.
The U.N. on Monday gave the go ahead to Iraq to pump 650,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil through its pipeline through Turkey and through its own Mina al-Bakr port in the south.
"The Mediterranean region is not a KPC market," he said.
Analysts say much of the Iraqi oil to be exported through Turkish facilities would be consumed in Turkey and the remainder would reach Mediterranean consumers such as Italy.
KPC's main markets are Asia and North America.
"There will be no impact on our contracts in the Asian markets. We have long-standing ties with our clients," said Shamm'a.
World supplies are currently less than global demand for oil, said Shamm'a. "The current strong prices have only one explanation which is that supply is less than demand."
"The market would be able to absorb such an amount," he said.
